Catholics teach that church and state are distinct, that the political community has its own dignity, and that the Church must be free to preach, worship, and serve. The Church does not seek to replace civil government. She claims the right to speak to public life on matters of justice and of the dignity of the person.

Historical arrangements have varied from establishment to sharp separation. Vatican II affirmed religious liberty as a civil right grounded in the dignity of the person. Catholics in public office remain bound by conscience. The Church does not reduce the Gospel to a party platform.
catholic.oaths:
Catholics may swear lawful oaths in court and in public office, calling God to witness the truth. Perjury is a grave sin. An oath that binds to evil is not to be kept. The name of God is not to be used lightly.

Religious profession and some offices in the Church also use vows and promises. These are not the same as civic oaths, but they share the seriousness of speech before God. Idle swearing is forbidden by the same reverence.
catholic.ordination_of_women:
The Catholic Church teaches that she has no authority to ordain women to the priesthood. The ministerial priesthood is reserved to baptized men, in fidelity to Christ's choice of the Twelve and to the Church's constant practice. John Paul II stated that this judgment is to be held definitively.

Women hold many offices and ministries: abbesses, doctors of the Church, chancellors, theologians, pastoral workers. None of that is the sacrament of Holy Orders as priests or bishops. Debate continues in some Catholic circles. Official teaching has not opened the priesthood to women.
catholic.headship:
Catholics speak of the complementarity of man and woman, equal in dignity and distinct in their gift. In marriage the tradition has spoken of the husband's headship as a call to self-giving, modeled on Christ, not as license to dominate. Ephesians 5 is read as mutual subordination in love, with a special burden of sacrifice on the husband.

Practice has often fallen short of that reading. Recent teaching stresses equal dignity and shared responsibility more than older household codes. The Church still does not treat sexual difference as a costume. It treats it as created meaning ordered to communion.
catholic.head_covering:
A chapel veil or mantilla is a custom of some Catholic women at Mass, once required by Latin canon law and no longer required after the code of 1983. Where it is used, it is a sign of reverence, not a sacrament. Eastern Catholic practice may differ.

No Catholic woman is bound to cover her head today in the Latin Church. No Catholic man is forbidden courtesy and modest dress. The old law is remembered by some as piety. It is not the present universal discipline.
catholic.roman_catholic_label:
Catholics ordinarily call themselves Catholic, members of the Catholic Church. Roman Catholic is accepted as a description of the Latin Church in communion with Rome, and many use it without strain. Some dislike it when it is used to imply that Catholic means a brand beside others of equal claim.

The Church of Rome is the church that presides in charity. Eastern churches in communion with the Pope are Catholic without being Latin. The name Catholic in the creed is the name this communion claims for herself.
catholic.separated_brethren:
Since Vatican II, Catholics officially speak of other baptized Christians as separated brethren. The phrase recognizes real baptism, real faith in Christ, and real gifts of the Spirit outside the visible Catholic Church, together with a break in full communion that the Church does not pretend is nothing.

Older language of heretics and schismatics remains in law for certain precise cases. Everyday Catholic speech after the council prefers brother and sister. The change is pastoral and doctrinal at once: unity is wounded, not absent in every respect.
catholic.true_church_claim:
Catholics believe that the Church of Christ continues fully in the Catholic Church. That is their true church claim. It is a claim about where the fullness of the apostolic faith, sacraments, and ministry reside, not a claim that every Catholic is better than every other Christian.

The same documents that make the claim also speak of elements of the Church present beyond her visible limits. Conversion to full communion is still sought. Contempt is not. The creed's one, holy, catholic, and apostolic Church is, for Catholics, this communion gathered around the successor of Peter.
